subject: Banking
title: Managing Employment
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Managing Employment.

hook.text: The Fed has a dual mandate: stable prices and maximum employment. Most central banks only target inflation.

buildup.text: When unemployment rises, the Fed cuts rates to stimulate borrowing, spending, and hiring. Cheap money creates jobs.

discovery.text: There's a tension: low unemployment can cause inflation, and fighting inflation can cause unemployment.

twist.text: The Phillips Curve looked stable until stagflation proved unemployment and inflation can rise together.

climax.text: Central banks influence employment through interest rates, but they can't create jobs directly.

punchline.text: Stable prices and full employment. The Fed's impossible balancing act.

quiz.question: What is the Fed's dual mandate?
